deviations.claim_in_article: “They could not tell if it was AI or a person” and “They did not realize it.”
deviations.issue: The article states that users in fact could not identify the caller and did not realize a human was speaking. The Ledger records that the test began without appropriate disclosure, but does not establish what users actually knew or realized.
deviations.explanation: The definitive claims about users’ awareness are not in the Ledger; absence of appropriate disclosure does not establish that users could not tell or did not realize. This is an unsupported factual assertion that strengthens the evidence. The Japanese source already makes the same implication, so this is not newly introduced by translation.
deviations.qualifier_text: “might think”; “If no one explained this clearly”

deviations.claim_in_article: “These calls were about trying to lower internet or cable fees.”
deviations.issue: The plural “calls” presents multiple calls about lowering internet or cable fees, while the Ledger records one reported individual case.
deviations.explanation: The Ledger describes one reported case; the article’s plural wording expands that case to multiple calls. The Japanese source refers to a phone call and one report, so the plurality is introduced in the English adaptation.
deviations.qualifier_text: “one employee’s report”; “this is only one report”
